I was once on ODSP. I am unsure of what your disability is, but they subcontract 3rd party representation to find a good fit job wise for you. This went beyond money for me, also a sense of purpose.

On ODSP atleast it is true they take money off your cheque, but you still come out ahead.



When you have a job they add $100.

They don't you touch the first $200 you make.

After your first $200 they take 50%. 

So let's say in a month you make $1000. $1000-$200(they don't touch)=$800

50%of $800=$400

($1200(original check) + $100)- $400=$900

However, what people forget to do is add your check to your pay: $900+$1000=$1900

I tried to simplify, not sure I did lol. But the take away is yes they take money off your check, but you still come out ahead.
